column1: # Scene 10280101 translations: "<dump index><TAB><english>". Indices are zero-based positions in the
# 10280101.json, 118 keys), so a key can never differ from what the game rendered. The keys are taken from
# the dump, never retyped, and the player name stays the %usernameusernameuserna% placeholder.
# The scene had no en.json at all ("Scenario translation load failed: 10280101"), so every line is new.
# Escapes: <LF> is a real line break. Sentences that also reach the interface table (the UI log reports
# scenario text too) keep the same wording there and here.

column2: ...Right. Ah, that's right.
I set out on a journey.
Together with my precious comrades.
Into that vast, vast space--
And then, I--
I committed a sin.
We... were created from the very start as disposable,<LF>existing just to gather resources...?
Don't be ridiculous!!
Earth?　Descendants of humanity?　Amatsukaze...?<LF>You mean we were born to be exploited by those incomprehensible people!?
Come on, calm down.
Surprisingly, just like Kotoha,<LF>Rami - the one most likely to lose her temper - said it in a calm voice.
Huh?　Aren't you angry!?
Obviously. I'm pissed as hell.
Then how about--
But you know, even if someone we have never met decides our future for us,<LF>we have no obligation to obey them. We just ignore it.
Honestly, my answer is "so what". Whatever happened long before we were born<LF>doesn't change who Rami and the others are now.
Rami and the others decide for Rami and the others! What we do from now on, we decide<LF>among ourselves! Nobody else interfere! That's all! ...or something like that?
...Hmph. I suppose you're right. I never thought I would hear that<LF>from a brat like you.
Huh!?　Who are you calling a brat, huh!? I won't take that from %usernameusernameuserna%'s<LF>tail-wagging, totally-smitten, pride-wrecked mutt of a dog!
Tail...!
Pride-wrecked mutt of a dog!?　Who is a dog!?<LF>You are starting to annoy me more than Izanami!
What a coincidence!　Rami finds you more annoying than that damn AI too!<LF>How about we settle this before we take down Izanami!?　Huh!?
...Honestly, could you two not fight even at a time like this?
Kotoha, I see you have no complaints about the smitten part...
Elena, I'll bite you!!
She really is a dog after all!?
But really, Rami is right. It is shocking,<LF>but I have not the slightest intention of letting Izanami have her way.
Our lives, our souls, our will--they are ours.
Right. I have no intention of giving it to anyone. Izanami's goal is not<LF>the same as ours. Why we were created does not matter.
I think so too. But precisely for that reason, Izanami, who toys with our lives<LF>like a tool, is still someone we have to stop.
That is right. I feel as though my resolve to settle things with Izanami<LF>has grown firmer.
Or rather, "to gather resources" aside,<LF>this story has become far too grand for me to follow...
So everything we learned at the Academy about evolution is a lie,<LF>and all our ancestors were created by Izanami?
..."Created" might be putting it a little inaccurately.
%usernameusernameuserna%...?
Everyone's ancestors come from the frozen fertilised eggs and the gene data<LF>library that were loaded onto the Amatsukaze.
%usernameusernameuserna%...?　What's this all of a sudden...
Even an emigration ship has a limit to how many people it can carry. ...After settlement, if only the crew<LF>had children, genetic diversity could have run short.
...To make up for that, the Amatsukaze carried something<LF>called a "Human Genetic Asset Library".
From there, the beings that are the ancestors of today's Zartum people were made.
%usernameusernameuserna%, was that just now--
Ah!　Master!　Does that mean you have "come back"!?
...Yeah.
Y-you came back...?
No way--
Yes!　Your me-mo-ries!　They are back!
Really!?
...The moment I heard about that "ship" from Pico, everything came back.<LF>I still cannot take it in as my own experience, though...
I was... a crew member<LF>of the interstellar emigration ship "Amatsukaze".
I came from somewhere other than Zartum Island,<LF>together with Izanami and many of my comrades.
But honestly, remembering it was not something to be glad about.<LF>Even though I finally remembered. Because--
Wait. So %usernameusernameuserna% is from<LF>that vessel...?　From what you say, it is from 10,000 years ago, is it not?
Yes, yes!　So that means %usernameusernameuserna% is,<LF>seriously, an unbelievable age...!
I did not actually spend 10,000 years awake.
There is a technology called cold sleep that puts a body into a frozen sleep,<LF>preserving it long-term while preventing ageing.
That is how I slept until quite recently. Along with the other crew members.
...Hearing that, one thing fell into place for me.<LF>When I admitted him to the Academy, I investigated him thoroughly.
...But in the end, there was no difference at all between our genetic structure and yours.
So there is no doubt that we share a common ancestor -<LF>the "Earthlings" who were driven from their homeland.
...But there was exactly one decisive difference<LF>between %usernameusernameuserna% and the rest of us.
The carbon atoms that make up the body--their radioactive isotope ratio.<LF>It was completely different.
Naturally, that would be the case.
............Hey, Harry. Do you understand what they are talking about...?<LF>Amatsukaze...?　What is that?
No, is this not the kind of thing that needs explaining from the very beginning...<LF>Well, I am about half lost myself, though.
...Same here. Times like this, it is inconvenient to be uneducated.
I will explain the gist of it later.
Thank you...!
The carbon isotope ratio is passed down through the food chain in an ecosystem.<LF>So if you grow up on Zartum Island, the value stays within a set range.
That is why, for example, the brat over there and I live lives<LF>that are completely different, yet our numbers do not differ much.
Oh, picking a fight again?　Because I'll take it.
Please do not start something at every opening in the middle of an important discussion...
Um, in short... an ecosystem's carbon isotope ratio,<LF>in the end, reflects the carbon isotope ratio contained in the land itself.
But only %usernameusernameuserna%,<LF>that value was clearly outside our range.
We know no world but Zartum Island. And in a place like that,<LF>we found a person who seemed to have lived in an environment unlike the island.
That is why Kotoha and I thought this:<LF>that this person came from "outside this world"--
Outside... the world...
So... the genes are the same, but the material forming your body is different.<LF>The environment you were born and raised in really was different from here.
That is right.
It does not feel real, somehow... Even when we first met,<LF>I could not tell at all that you were "different" from us.
First met...
Different or not, it is only the environment you were raised in.<LF>As living beings we are the same. It is no wonder you could not tell.
...Um, excuse me. May I have a moment?
What is it?
I am sorry to derail the conversation, but...
There is one thing that bothers me. When we first met,<LF>%usernameusernameuserna% said something.
This world is about to be destroyed...
In the end, did that mean Izanami taking the resources will leave our society<LF>unable to function... was that the right reading?
It just stayed with me, somehow...
Because it is true that resource depletion from Izanami's plundering<LF>would lead to the extreme decline of Zartum civilisation.
Humanity surely cannot keep its current numbers and will decline.<LF>A very harsh, sad future awaits.
But, to take it to an extreme... if civilisation fell back to the Stone Age,<LF>I think mere survival might still be possible.
...So "destruction" sounds like an exaggeration, then.
Yes. Though it is also possible that %usernameusernameuserna%<LF>deliberately chose that wording...
Maybe it is related to the "calamity"<LF>Pico mentioned earlier... was that it?
Now that you mention it, Izanami said something strange too.
I do not recommend my destruction.<LF>"Rather, it would become irreversible for this world," she said.
Mm. At the time I thought it was just a threat... a bluff...
Oh my... does that mean there is a crisis in the world we have not noticed yet--<LF>not just resource depletion, but something else as well?
What!?　There is more!?
Disposable--does this mean it is not simply about civilisation collapsing,<LF>but contains something even worse?
If %usernameusernameuserna% has his memories back,<LF>surely he knows something...?
%usernameusernameuserna%...<LF>When the Amatsukaze is repaired, what will become of us?
...Let me explain in order.
To start with, the words I said before, the "calamity",<LF>and Izanami's "irreversible thing" are all separate matters.
Separate... matters?
I-I give up, I cannot follow any of this...
Sorry for the confusion, everyone.<LF>First, "defeating" Izanami means--
Piko-piko-piin!　Everyone, this is serious!
What is it!?　We are in the middle of something important...!
Izanami's main server has vanished!!
What did you say!?
The vault we are heading for is already empty!!
